rows.probe: direct submission of a caller-supplied candidate: result value, and every durable row and event written
rows.note: Return the proposal-id string: it is request-free, gives the caller the review handle, and avoids freezing a richer result before M3.4.

rows.probe: source-backed submission: the source runs exactly once, and the durable footprint against P01
rows.note: A per-call source runs once and then enters the same one-request, one-proposal, one-event persistence path as a direct candidate.

rows.probe: the source runs OUTSIDE every open transaction: connection.in_transaction observed during propose
rows.note: The same injected connection spy observed an active transaction in its positive control and zero open connections during source invocation.

rows.probe: the source raises CandidateSourceError: exact public class and message, zero durable rows, zero events
rows.note: A source-raised CandidateSourceError is replaced by one stable public class and text; full-ledger and event snapshots remain identical.

rows.probe: the source raises an arbitrary Exception: identical public text to P04, nothing internal leaked
rows.note: An arbitrary RuntimeError produces the exact P04 class and text, with no cause, context, durable mutation, event, or internal string exposure.

rows.probe: source-backed submission with no candidate_source configured: exact class and message
rows.note: This signature accepts the source per call, so source-backed submission succeeds without System configuration; there is no missing-config error.

rows.probe: direct submission while a candidate_source IS configured: the source must not be invoked
rows.note: Direct candidates ignore System configuration, and a distinct per-call source is authoritative; legacy handle proves the configured counter is live.

rows.probe: both candidate and source supplied, and neither supplied: exact class and message, or the signature that makes it unreachable
